key_insight: Entrance effects in lab-scale DCMD are Reynolds-number dependent: near-inlet vortices can either strengthen or weaken temperature polarization depending on flow rate and geometry.
engineering_relevance: Membrane distillation module design and heat-transfer correlations must account for entrance geometry and operating Reynolds number, rather than using a single constant correction.
method: 3D CFD of direct contact membrane distillation modules
Sweep of inlet Reynolds number from 10 to 1000
Varied side-chamber length and main-channel height to isolate geometry effects
evidence_signal: Simulations showed counter-rotating streamwise vortices near the entrance across all geometries, with persistence and TP deviation increasing at higher Reynolds numbers and changing sign relative to a straight-channel baseline.
watch_item: Because the entrance bias changes with both geometry and Reynolds number, corrections calibrated at one operating condition may not transfer reliably to others.
paper_title: Reynolds-number-dependent entrance bias in temperature polarization of lab-scale membrane distillation
